definition: Fine-tuning a model on (instruction, response) pairs so it follows natural-language requests reliably.
details: Instruction tuning turns raw text models into assistants by training them on diverse human instructions and expected responses. FLAN showed that fine-tuning across many tasks phrased as instructions lets a model answer unseen tasks in zero-shot form, a step that foreshadowed the assistant behavior of later chat models.

explainer.lead: Instruction tuning fine-tunes a model on instruction-response pairs so it follows natural-language requests reliably. It turns raw text models into assistants, and FLAN showed that tuning across many tasks phrased as instructions lets a model answer unseen tasks zero-shot.

tiers.eli5: It is training a model on lots of 'do this' requests together with good answers, so later it can handle new requests it has never seen.
tiers.practitioner: Engineers fine-tune on diverse human instructions and expected responses to produce assistant behaviour. A pitfall is expecting good answers on unseen tasks without the broad, varied instruction coverage that makes zero-shot transfer work.
tiers.paperLevel: Fine-tuning a model on (instruction, response) pairs so it follows natural-language requests reliably. FLAN showed that fine-tuning across many tasks phrased as instructions lets a model answer unseen tasks in zero-shot form.

explainer.example: After instruction tuning across many tasks phrased as instructions, a model can answer a new task it was never trained on by following the request directly.

citation.title: Finetuned Language Models Are Zero-Shot Learners
